A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and scientific appendices A–G. The removed checklist and broken cross-references in v2 do not prevent reliable content matching.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original optimization experiments, classification accuracies, and sensitivity analyses on synthetic distributions, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain original optimization experiments and clean/adversarial classification results, including Table 1 and Figures 1 and A2–A6.

M1.justification: The single-layer linear transformer, masked attention, adversarial pretraining objective, and parameter solutions are unchanged. The new Z_delta and Z_0 notation distinguishes perturbed and clean inputs without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic training and test distributions and binary classification tasks from MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10. No dataset, domain, or evaluated test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figures A4–A6 retain the same comparison between normally and adversarially pretrained transformers. No additional comparison method is empirically evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains the preprocessing, training budgets, perturbation settings, synthetic sampling procedures, and evaluation sizes. The 45 image-class pairs and synthetic batches with 1,000 demonstrations and 1,000 queries are unchanged.

E4.justification: The feature-statistics analysis and sweeps over perturbation size, robust/non-robust/irrelevant dimensions, and demonstration count are retained in Figures A2 and A4–A6. No new ablation, robustness test, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same standard-deviation bands across synthetic batches or 45 binary classification pairs. There is no change in seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 1 repeats the same numerical results, including MNIST clean/robust accuracies of 94/4 for the standard model and 93/72 for the adversarial model. Figures 1 and A2–A6 retain the same graphics and findings.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, theorem bounds, and appendix derivations are retained. However, the explanation after Theorem 3.5 corrects a mathematical inference: v1 says the upper bound's sign determines success, whereas v2 only infers failure when that bound is nonpositive.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims of robust adaptation through clean in-context demonstrations, preferential use of robust features, reduced sensitivity to irrelevant dimensions, high-dimensional failure, an accuracy–robustness trade-off, and greater demonstration requirements. v2 reorganizes their emphasis without changing these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v2 expands the architectural and pretraining-cost limitations, including absent softmax/multilayer characteristics and proposed financing through licensing or API fees. It removes v1's suggestion that multilayer analysis might permit robustness under any conditions. Section 3.5 also changes heavier reliance on robust features to the less precise claim that non-robust features are discarded.

D1.justification: Hardware, optimization details, preprocessing, and use of theoretical parameter solutions remain unchanged in Appendix C. The standalone reproducibility statement repeats the supplementary-code information already present in v1's checklist; both PDFs provide the same repository link.

R1.justification: v2 adds Schmidt et al. (2018), 'Adversarially robust generalization requires more data,' to connect demonstration requirements with an established robustness challenge. The remaining related-work coverage is largely retained; switching to author–year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten, and Positive/Negative Results become Universal Robustness/Open Challenges. The checklist is replaced by short reproducibility and LLM-use statements. v2 also introduces seven unresolved '??' cross-references in Appendices D and E.

P2.justification: The document restyles titles, headings, and page headers and reflows existing material. Table 1 moves from page 10 to page 9, and Figure A4 moves from page 21 to page 22. Figure designs and table structure remain unchanged, while some theorem boxes become split across pages.

improvement.justification: Clearer headline scope, fuller limitations, and the corrected inference after Theorem 3.5 provide modest benefits. However, v2 introduces seven broken proof references and replaces feature reweighting with a less accurate 'discards' explanation in Section 3.5. With the experimental evidence and formal results retained, these opposing changes leave the net quality direction uncertain.
